Replying to: m01
Cc: none
Subject: Re: Blister packs for my mother - new patient

Dear Mr Kerrigan,

Thank you for getting in touch, and welcome — we would be glad to look after your mother. I'm sorry to hear about her fall, and I hope her week in hospital has gone as smoothly as it could. I've answered your questions in the order you asked them.

1. Weekly blister packs — yes, we prepare them. Your mother's would be a seven-day pack, four times a day. There is no charge for the packaging itself; she would only pay our usual dispensing fee, and since she is 81, the Ontario Drug Benefit covers most of that.

2. Delivery — yes, we deliver to her building. Our delivery days are Tuesdays and Fridays, 2 to 6 pm, free within 8 km, and her condo is well inside that. Thursday isn't a delivery day, so for the first pack you can either pick it up at the store or I can arrange a one-off drop on the Saturday before 1 pm. After that we can settle into the Tuesday/Friday routine, whichever suits her.

3. Moving her prescriptions — this is straightforward, and she doesn't need to sign anything for the transfers. We just need the name and address of her current pharmacy on Dundas and her OHIP number, and we will contact them ourselves.

4. Speaking with you — yes, I would be happy to call you in the evening to go over her new medication list. My direct line is 905-555-0148 ext 2, and I am in the store Monday to Friday, 9 to 6.

One thing I should explain before we get into the medication details. Because your mother is an adult patient, we need her permission on file before we can discuss her medications with anyone else, including family. It isn't meant to be a hurdle — it's there to protect her privacy and keep her in control of her own health information. We use a short signed form called a Family Communication Consent. She can sign it when she comes to the store, or we can send it home with the driver and she can sign it then. Once it is on file, I can speak with you freely.

I would also like to offer a MedsCheck at her home during her first week back — a sit-down review of everything she is taking, about 20 minutes, with me. I can come Monday or Tuesday after 6 pm, whichever works best for you both.

On timing: the first blister packs need about 48 hours once we have all her prescriptions in hand, including the transfers. If the hospital can fax the discharge prescriptions to us early on Thursday, we can realistically have the packs ready for Saturday. They will not be ready on the day she is discharged, so could you confirm with the discharge team that she has an interim supply to cover her until Saturday? It would also help if you could go through each dose with them before she leaves, so everyone is clear on what she is taking in those first few days.

If you can send me the old pharmacy's details and her OHIP number, and ask the hospital to fax us Thursday morning, I will get everything moving on our end.

Kind regards,
Rania Haddad
Pharmacist, Erindale Park Pharmacy
905-555-0148 ext 2
